facts.statement: Hudsonelpidia was a small ichthyosaur belonging to the parvipelvian group, found in British Columbia, Canada.
facts.quote: Hudsonelpidia is an extinct genus of small parvipelvian ichthyosaur known from British Columbia of Canada.

facts.statement: Chris McGowan named the genus Hudsonelpidia in 1995, with Hudsonelpidia brevirostris as the type species.
facts.quote: Hudsonelpidia was named by Chris McGowan in 1995 and the type species is Hudsonelpidia brevirostris.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Hudsonelpidia is a nearly complete holotype skeleton measuring less than 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Hudsonelpidia is known only from the holotype, a nearly complete skeleton measuring less than 2 m long.

facts.statement: Fossils of Hudsonelpidia date to the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected in the Jewitt Spur locality from the Pardonet Formation, dating to the middle Norian stage of the Late Triassic, about 210 million years ago.

facts.statement: The fossils were discovered on the northern shore of the Peace Reach branch of Williston Lake.
facts.quote: It was found on the northern shore of the Peace Reach branch of Williston Lake.

facts.statement: The family Hudsonelpidiidae was established to include the genus Hudsonelpidia.
Hudsonelpidia is classified within the unranked group Parvipelvia.
The holotype specimen of Hudsonelpidia preserves the skull in addition to being a nearly complete skeleton.
facts.quote: Hudsonelpidia es conocido solo por el holotipo, un esqueleto casi completo que preseva el cráneo.

facts.statement: Hudsonelpidia shows a very stable position in many cladistic analyses.
facts.quote: Hudsonelpidia tiene una posición muy estable en muchos análisis cladísticos.

facts.statement: The time range for Hudsonelpidia is estimated between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
